bolasterone-finaject.summary: An oral veterinary steroid that physique users have discussed for mass and strength; published material is mostly anti-doping detection work.

quick.overview:
Bolasterone is an oral methylated androgen originally made for veterinary use. People who write about it in steroid histories describe it as a mass and strength compound, with a low-to-moderate anabolic-to-androgenic ratio.

The chain is the usual androgen one: it activates the androgen receptor, which drives muscle protein gain, and more muscle and strength change how a physique looks. Most of what has been published about it concerns detection chemistry in doping control, and no human trials were found.
quick.how: In steroid histories it appears as an oral compound taken by mouth in cycles alongside training and diet, with muscle and strength gains discussed over weeks. It is rarely encountered today and is known mostly as a name in anti-doping literature.
quick.risks: No human safety data exist, so risks are inferred from other 17-alkylated oral steroids, which are associated with liver strain, hormone suppression and cholesterol changes. It is banned by WADA and controlled in some countries such as Brazil.

angle.text: Bolasterone is an oral methylated androgen aimed at more muscle and strength: it activates the androgen receptor, which speeds muscle protein gain and fills out the physique. Published work on it is mostly anti-doping detection chemistry, so its physique use rests on class effects.

chlorodehydromethyltestosterone-turinabo.summary: An oral steroid of East German doping fame that lifters use for lean, dry muscle gain with little water retention.

quick.overview:
Turinabol is an oral anabolic steroid, a chlorinated version of metandienone, known for its place in East Germany's state doping programme. Lifters favour it for lean, dry-looking muscle with less water retention.

It activates the androgen receptor, which raises muscle protein gain. It was in clinical use from 1965 to 1994, and its long-lasting urinary metabolites, identified in 2012, allowed old Olympic samples to be re-tested. Published research is mostly metabolism and detection studies, plus isolated case reports of harm.
quick.how: People use it as a tablet taken by mouth in cycles alongside heavy training and a calorie surplus or cut, often stacked with other compounds. Lifters describe gains building over several weeks.
quick.risks: Documented harms are limited to case reports and general anabolic-steroid concerns, including liver strain, hormone suppression and a case report of a testicular tumour after high-dose use. It is banned in sport and controlled in the US, UK and Brazil.

angle.text: Turinabol is an oral steroid used for lean, dry muscle gain: it activates the androgen receptor, speeding muscle protein gain with little water retention. Its history and detection science are well documented, while clinical trials for muscle or appearance have not been published.

clostebol-4-chlorotestosterone.summary: A chlorinated testosterone known from skin creams and doping cases that bodybuilders discuss for lean mass.

quick.overview:
Clostebol is testosterone with a chlorine atom added. It is sold in some countries as a topical wound-healing product, and bodybuilders have discussed it as an injectable ester for modest lean mass gains.

It activates the androgen receptor, and the chlorine is said to stop conversion to DHT and estrogen, which proponents link to a leaner, less puffy look. Its anabolic effect is described as modest. Published work is dominated by anti-doping analysis, and no trials test it for muscle or appearance.
quick.how: Physique users describe it as an injectable ester used in cycles, often alongside other compounds, with lean gains developing over weeks. In medicine it is a skin cream or spray for wounds.
quick.risks: Risks are inferred from anabolic steroids in general, as clostebol-specific human data for physique use are lacking. It is prohibited in sport, controlled in the US, Canada and Brazil, and some positive tests have been traced to accidental skin contamination.

angle.text: Clostebol is a chlorinated testosterone discussed for lean muscle support: it activates the androgen receptor with a mild anabolic effect and no DHT or estrogen conversion. The muscle use rests on class effects and user reports, and it is best known from skin creams and doping cases.

danazol.summary: A prescription steroid for endometriosis and angioedema that is mentioned in muscle forums for its weak androgenic effects.

quick.overview:
Danazol is an oral steroid prescribed for endometriosis, hereditary angioedema and some blood disorders. Bodybuilding forum users mention it for its weak androgenic effects and a possible small lean-mass benefit.

It suppresses LH and FSH and displaces hormones from SHBG, which raises free testosterone, and it also binds the androgen receptor. It has been studied for those medical conditions; no studies have tested it for appearance.
quick.how: Medically it is a daily oral prescription taken for months under a doctor's supervision. In muscle communities it is mentioned as an add-on to other hormone protocols.
quick.risks: Acne, excess hair growth, weight gain, lipid changes, raised liver enzymes and voice deepening are reported, and the voice and other masculinising effects can be permanent. It virilises female fetuses, is contraindicated in pregnancy and is prescription-only.

angle.text: Danazol is a prescription steroid that forum users mention for a possible small lean-mass effect: it lowers SHBG and gonadotropins and has weak androgenic activity. It is studied for endometriosis and angioedema, and no study has tested it for appearance.

tibolone-livial.summary: A menopause drug with weak androgenic activity that some forum users discuss as a mild anabolic.

quick.overview:
Tibolone is a prescription hormone therapy for menopause symptoms and osteoporosis in many countries, though not the US. Some bodybuilding forum posters discuss it as a mild anabolic with a possible lean-mass effect.

It is a prodrug whose metabolites act on estrogen, progesterone and androgen receptors in tissue-selective ways and lower SHBG. It has been tested in large randomised trials for menopause symptoms and bone; no study has tested it for appearance or muscle.
quick.how: Medically it is a daily oral tablet for postmenopausal women. In muscle contexts it is mentioned as a milder add-on rather than a main compound.
quick.risks: Trials and reviews report increased stroke risk in older women, higher breast cancer recurrence in survivors, and endometrial and bleeding concerns. Acne and facial hair occur in some women. It is a Canadian Schedule IV controlled substance and banned by WADA.

angle.text: Tibolone is a menopause drug that some users discuss as a mild anabolic for lean mass, via weak androgenic activity. It has been trialled extensively for menopause symptoms and bone, but not for looks.

gestrinone.summary: A weakly androgenic endometriosis steroid, parent of the THG designer steroid, discussed for a leaner, harder look.

quick.overview:
Gestrinone is a prescription steroid used in some countries for endometriosis. Bodybuilding circles mention it for a leaner, harder look because of its weak androgenic and anabolic activity together with antiestrogen and antiprogestogen action.

It binds the progesterone receptor strongly and the androgen receptor more weakly, suppresses ovarian steroid production and lowers SHBG, which raises free testosterone. It is also the chemical precursor of the designer steroid THG. Published clinical research is on endometriosis, not on muscle or body composition.
quick.how: Medically it is taken orally on a regular schedule for endometriosis under a doctor's care. In performance circles it is mentioned as a supporting compound in hormone protocols.
quick.risks: Reported effects include acne, oily skin, hair loss, hirsutism, weight gain, menstrual suppression and voice deepening, some of which may be irreversible. It is contraindicated in pregnancy, banned in sport and not approved in the US.

angle.text: Gestrinone is an endometriosis steroid that performance circles discuss for a leaner, harder look, through weak androgenic and antiestrogen action. Clinical research covers gynecological conditions, and nothing has been studied for appearance.

testolactone-teslac.summary: A discontinued steroidal aromatase inhibitor once used for breast cancer, discussed by bodybuilders for limiting estrogen.

quick.overview:
Testolactone (Teslac) was a prescription aromatase inhibitor approved in the US in 1970 for advanced breast cancer and discontinued in 2008. Bodybuilders have discussed it for limiting estrogen during steroid use, aiming for less water retention and a drier look.

It blocks the aromatase enzyme that converts androgens to estrogens, with a lowering of estradiol that is modest compared with newer drugs. It was also studied in children with precocious puberty and in infertile men; no trial has examined it for appearance.
quick.how: Medically it was an oral daily drug for postmenopausal breast cancer. It is no longer available, and newer aromatase inhibitors have taken over the roles it was discussed for.
quick.risks: Reported effects include tingling, aches, hair loss, nausea and vomiting, with rarer allergic reactions and edema. It is no longer available for medical use.

angle.text: Testolactone is a discontinued aromatase inhibitor that bodybuilders discussed for limiting estrogen: less conversion of androgens to estrogen means less water retention and a drier look. It was studied for breast cancer, and nothing was tested for looks.

formestane-lentaron.summary: An injectable steroidal aromatase inhibitor for breast cancer, discussed in bodybuilding for controlling estrogen.

quick.overview:
Formestane (Lentaron) is an injectable steroidal aromatase inhibitor used for postmenopausal breast cancer. Bodybuilding discussion mentions it for suppressing estrogen from anabolic steroids or prohormones, aiming at lower gynecomastia risk and a drier look.

It irreversibly binds aromatase and blocks estrogen synthesis, and it converts to 4-hydroxytestosterone, a weak androgen. It has been studied for cancer; no trial has tested it for appearance.
quick.how: Medically it was given as a clinician-administered depot injection. It is not orally active, and the European injectable has been withdrawn.
quick.risks: Available sources give little on side effects. It was never FDA-approved and the injectable has been withdrawn in Europe.

angle.text: Formestane is an injectable aromatase inhibitor discussed in bodybuilding circles for controlling estrogen: lower estrogen means less gynecomastia risk and a drier look. It has been studied for breast cancer, and nothing has been tested for appearance.

fadrozole.summary: A nonsteroidal aromatase inhibitor used for breast cancer in Japan and in lab research, mentioned as an estrogen blocker.

quick.overview:
Fadrozole (Afema) is an oral aromatase inhibitor used for breast cancer in Japan. Bodybuilding circles mention it as an estrogen blocker, aiming at lower estrogen, less gynecomastia risk and a drier look.

It reversibly binds the heme group of aromatase and reduces conversion of androgens to estrogens by about 80 to 90 percent at tested doses. Beyond oncology it is mostly a lab tool for blocking estrogen in fish, birds and rodents. No human trial has examined it for appearance.
quick.how: Medically it is a prescription oral drug in Japan. Outside oncology it appears mainly in animal and lab research.
quick.risks: Sources give little detail on its side effects. It is prescription-only and not approved in most countries.

angle.text: Fadrozole is an aromatase inhibitor mentioned as an estrogen blocker for a drier look and lower gynecomastia risk. It is used for breast cancer in Japan and as a lab tool, and no human trial has tested it for appearance.

vorozole.summary: A discontinued third-generation aromatase inhibitor now used as a brain-imaging tracer, occasionally mentioned as an estrogen blocker.

quick.overview:
Vorozole is an oral aromatase inhibitor developed for cancer. It occasionally comes up in physique forums as an estrogen blocker, with the aim of less water retention and a leaner look.

It competitively blocks the aromatase enzyme, reducing estrogen synthesis. Development stopped after a trial showed no survival difference from megestrol acetate, and it was never marketed. Today it is best known as a carbon-11 PET tracer for mapping aromatase in the human brain. No trial has tested it for appearance.
quick.how: It is not a marketed product. Its present use is as a research radiotracer in brain imaging.
quick.risks: Sources do not describe its adverse effects. It is an investigational compound without marketing approval.

angle.text: Vorozole is an aromatase inhibitor that occasionally comes up as an estrogen blocker: less estrogen synthesis means less water retention and a leaner look. It was studied for cancer and is now a brain-imaging tracer, and nothing has been tested for looks.

aminoglutethimide-cytadren.summary: An old adrenal-steroid and aromatase blocker that bodybuilders used before contests to cut cortisol and estrogen.

quick.overview:
Aminoglutethimide (Cytadren) began as an epilepsy drug and was later used for Cushing's syndrome and hormone-sensitive cancers. Some bodybuilders have used it before contests to cut cortisol and estrogen, aiming for a leaner, drier look.

It inhibits several steroid-synthesis enzymes, notably P450scc in the adrenal gland and aromatase, lowering cortisol and estrogen. Wikipedia notes that few users report positive experiences. No trials have tested it for appearance.
quick.how: Medically it is an oral drug taken under supervision with corticosteroid replacement. In physique circles it has been used in short pre-contest phases, though users report it as unpleasant.
quick.risks: Lethargy is the most common effect; rash, low blood pressure, liver toxicity and adrenal insufficiency are reported. Medical use pairs it with corticosteroid cover. It is marketed in only a few countries.

angle.text: Aminoglutethimide blocks adrenal steroid synthesis and aromatase, and bodybuilders have used it before contests aiming to cut cortisol and estrogen for a leaner, drier look. It has been studied for Cushing's syndrome and cancer, not for physique.

atd-1-4-6-androstatrienedione.summary: A prohormone-era supplement aromatase inhibitor, discussed in muscle circles as a way to limit estrogen conversion.

quick.overview:
ATD is a steroid-like supplement ingredient sold over the counter in the prohormone era, reportedly until around 2009. Muscle-building circles discuss it for limiting estrogen conversion, aiming for less water retention and fewer gynecomastia concerns.

It is described as an irreversible aromatase inhibitor, binding the enzyme that makes estrogen from androgens and inactivating it. Support comes from enzyme studies and an old monkey study; no human trial of its effects on muscle, gynecomastia or appearance was found.
quick.how: It was sold as an oral supplement, usually alongside prohormones or steroids during a cycle. Products carried varied names.
quick.risks: No human safety data were found. It is banned in sport and can reportedly cause a positive boldenone test. Products under varied names can be hard to identify.

angle.text: ATD is a prohormone-era aromatase inhibitor used to limit conversion of androgens to estrogen, aiming for less water and fewer gynecomastia concerns. Lab data support the mechanism, and no human trial has tested the look-related claims.

6-oxo-4-androstene-3-6-17-trione.summary: A prohormone-era aromatase inhibitor used to limit estrogen; one uncontrolled study showed hormone shifts and no body-composition change.

quick.overview:
6-OXO is an oral supplement ingredient described as an irreversible aromatase inhibitor. Steroid and prohormone users take it to limit estrogen rise and gynecomastia risk and to speed recovery after cycles, aiming at a higher testosterone-to-estrogen ratio and a leaner muscular look.

It is reported to permanently inactivate aromatase, lowering estradiol and raising LH and testosterone. The main human study, a 2007 eight-week trial in resistance-trained men, was uncontrolled and partly industry-funded; it found large rises in free testosterone and DHT but no change in body composition.
quick.how: It is taken as an oral supplement, typically during or after steroid or prohormone cycles. Users describe it as part of a recovery or estrogen-control routine.
quick.risks: The FDA stated products containing it are adulterated, and Health Canada warned in 2008 of a blood-clotting risk. Acne is a listed possible effect. It is banned by WADA.

angle.text: 6-OXO is used by steroid and prohormone users who say it limits estrogen rise, supports recovery and keeps the muscle look leaner. A 2007 uncontrolled study showed hormone shifts without body-composition change.

damiana-extract-turnera-diffusa.summary: A traditional aphrodisiac herb taken by some as a natural anti-aromatase, with lab data on its constituents.

quick.overview:
Damiana is a shrub used in teas and liqueurs and sold as an herbal supplement. Some supplement users take it as a natural anti-aromatase to support testosterone, aiming for slightly lower estrogen conversion and a leaner, more muscular look.

A 2008 laboratory study reported that flavonoids in damiana, such as pinocembrin and acacetin, inhibit aromatase. No human trial of damiana alone on estrogen or appearance was found.
quick.how: It is taken as a tea, tincture or capsule, often inside combination hormone-support products. Users do not describe a clear timeline.
quick.risks: Safety data are limited in the sources reviewed. Products may contain false damiana (Turnera ulmifolia), and combination products make effects hard to attribute.

angle.text: Damiana is a traditional herb that supplement users take as a natural anti-aromatase, aiming for slightly lower estrogen and a leaner look. A 2008 lab study found anti-aromatase constituents; human trials of the extract alone are absent.

white-button-mushroom-extract.summary: A common food whose extracts inhibit aromatase in lab assays, used by some for a better testosterone-to-estrogen balance.

quick.overview:
White button mushroom is an everyday food. Users aiming for a better testosterone-to-estrogen balance include it, or its extracts, among natural aromatase inhibitors, hoping for lower estrogen and a leaner look.

Extracts have been reported to reduce aromatase activity in enzyme assays, with white mushroom showing the greatest effect. A 2009 case-control study in southeast China linked higher mushroom intake to lower breast cancer incidence. Human trials found were registered for cancer-related questions; none addressed appearance.
quick.how: People eat it as a regular food or take concentrated extract capsules. No appearance timeline is described.
quick.risks: As a common food it is widely eaten; safety data for concentrated extracts were not reviewed in depth. Wild lookalikes such as the death cap are dangerous, which concerns foraging rather than cultivated product.

angle.text: White button mushroom extract is used by people aiming for a better testosterone-to-estrogen balance, via aromatase inhibition seen in lab assays. Human work is cancer-focused, not about looks.

afimoxifene-4-hydroxytamoxifen.summary: The active form of tamoxifen, studied as a breast gel in women and discussed by some men for gynecomastia.

quick.overview:
Afimoxifene is the active metabolite of tamoxifen, formulated as a gel applied to the breast. Some men consider it for gynecomastia, aiming for less breast tissue growth and a flatter chest.

As a SERM it blocks estrogen at estrogen receptors in breast tissue, and applied topically the aim is local effects. Trials have been in women for breast pain, density and cancer settings, and the mastalgia trial was designed around avoiding the systemic effects of oral tamoxifen. No published trial in men with gynecomastia was found.
quick.how: It is investigational and designed as a gel rubbed onto the breast. Gynecomastia users discuss it as a topical alternative to oral SERMs.
quick.risks: It is not approved anywhere in the sources reviewed. Side-effect details for the gel were not reviewed in depth.

angle.text: Afimoxifene is the active form of tamoxifen, used as a breast gel; some men consider it for gynecomastia, since blocking estrogen receptors in the breast means less tissue growth and a flatter chest. Trials have been in women, not men.

raloxifene-evista.summary: A prescription SERM approved for women's bone and breast risk, used off-label by men to shrink gynecomastia.

quick.overview:
Raloxifene is a prescription SERM approved for osteoporosis and breast cancer risk reduction in postmenopausal women. Men use it off-label to shrink gynecomastia tissue and flatten the chest, including puberty-onset cases, often alongside or after tamoxifen.

It blocks estrogen action in breast tissue and mimics it in bone. Forum posters report shrinkage and some regrowth after stopping. Published evidence for this use is limited to small studies, such as a retrospective review in adolescent boys.
quick.how: It is a daily oral tablet taken for months. Users describe gradual shrinkage and often continue until results plateau.
quick.risks: The label carries a boxed warning for blood clots and stroke death; common effects include hot flashes, leg cramps and swelling. It is prescription-only, contraindicated in pregnancy, and not approved for men.

angle.text: Raloxifene is a SERM that men use off-label to shrink gynecomastia: it blocks estrogen action in breast tissue, which reduces gland tissue and flattens the chest. Forum posters report shrinkage and regrowth after stopping, and published evidence is limited to small studies.

toremifene.summary: A tamoxifen-like SERM approved for breast cancer and used off-label for gynecomastia and post-cycle recovery.

quick.overview:
Toremifene is a prescription SERM closely related to tamoxifen, approved for advanced breast cancer in postmenopausal women. Men use it off-label as an estrogen blocker for gynecomastia and post-cycle recovery, aiming at a flatter chest.

It blocks estrogen's effect in breast tissue while acting partly like estrogen in bone. Medical literature reports improvement of gynecomastia in men and prevention of bicalutamide-induced breast enlargement. No controlled trial of aesthetic or post-cycle use in healthy men was found.
quick.how: It is a daily oral tablet. In bodybuilding and hormone-therapy contexts it is mentioned as an alternative to tamoxifen.
quick.risks: The US label carries a boxed warning for QT prolongation and arrhythmia, plus warnings on liver toxicity, uterine effects and pregnancy. Common effects include hot flashes, sweating and nausea. It is prescription-only.

angle.text: Toremifene is a tamoxifen-like SERM that men use off-label for gynecomastia and post-cycle recovery: blocking estrogen in breast tissue shrinks gland growth and flattens the chest. Reported benefit comes from medical settings such as men on antiandrogen therapy.

fulvestrant-faslodex.summary: An injectable pure antiestrogen used for breast cancer that occasionally comes up in gynecomastia discussions.

quick.overview:
Fulvestrant is a prescription injection that blocks and breaks down the estrogen receptor, approved for hormone receptor-positive breast cancer in postmenopausal women. It is sometimes named in hormone discussions as a pure estrogen blocker, with a possible flatter male chest as the goal.

It binds the estrogen receptor and marks it for destruction, reducing estrogen signaling in breast tissue. Published research covers cancer and rare pediatric conditions, and no study addresses appearance.
quick.how: It is given as a clinician-administered intramuscular injection under medical care.
quick.risks: Reported effects include injection-site reactions, nausea, weakness, raised liver enzymes and clots. The label warns about bleeding risk, hepatic impairment and fetal harm. It is prescription-only.

angle.text: Fulvestrant is an injectable pure antiestrogen that occasionally comes up for gynecomastia: degrading estrogen receptors reduces estrogen signaling in breast tissue, which could mean a flatter chest. It is used for breast cancer, and no study addresses appearance.

bazedoxifene.summary: A menopause and osteoporosis SERM used for bone protection and hot flushes, sometimes researched by men among estrogen modulators.

quick.overview:
Bazedoxifene is a prescription SERM used for osteoporosis prevention and, combined with conjugated estrogens, for menopausal symptoms. It sits among the estrogen-modulating drugs that men sometimes research, though no source ties it to appearance.

It binds estrogen receptors and acts like estrogen in bone while blocking it in tissues such as the uterus. A 3-year randomised trial in women with osteoporosis found fewer new vertebral fractures than placebo.
quick.how: It is a daily oral tablet; in the US it is sold combined with conjugated estrogens as Duavee for menopausal symptoms.
quick.risks: The combination product carries a boxed warning for endometrial cancer, cardiovascular disorders and probable dementia. Common effects include muscle spasms, nausea and diarrhea. It is prescription-only and contraindicated in pregnancy.

angle.text: Bazedoxifene is a SERM that acts on estrogen receptors for bone protection and hot flushes, and it sits among the estrogen modulators men sometimes research. Its published research concerns bone and menopause, with no appearance studies.
